official_sources: Smooth snake and sand lizard mitigation licence A46
Protected species science education conservation licence A29
Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017
Natural Environment and Rural Communities Act 2006

official_measurement_examples.name: EPS reptile distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Smooth snakes and sand lizards are European protected species with breeding and resting-place protections under the Habitats Regulations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Other native reptile distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Adders, grass snakes, common lizards and slow worms have different protection under the Wildlife and Countryside Act and must not be treated as having the identical A46 regime.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning standing advice
official_measurement_examples.fact: Reptile standing advice is a material planning consideration and was updated 7 April 2025.

official_measurement_examples.name: A46 mitigation trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: A46 is required where work would otherwise unlawfully affect smooth snakes or sand lizards through specified protected activities.

official_measurement_examples.name: A46 evidence pack
official_measurement_examples.fact: A46 applications require an application form, method statement, work schedule and reasoned statement plus references where applicable.

official_measurement_examples.name: A46 decision period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states it will decide an A46 mitigation application within 30 working days after receiving the application.

official_measurement_examples.name: Survey licence distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A29 is the survey, research or conservation route for applicable protected species and is distinct from A46 development mitigation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Reptile survey or licensing does not itself grant planning permission, prove reptile absence or determine parcel development capacity.

core_rules: reptile protection law is not proof reptiles are present on a parcel
reptile survey result is not planning permission
planning permission is not an A46 mitigation licence
A46 applies to smooth snakes and sand lizards rather than every native reptile
common native reptile protection must not be represented as identical EPS licensing
A29 survey licence is distinct from A46 development mitigation
planning standing advice is not a planning decision
reasoned statement is licence evidence not a planning grant
historic reptile survey must retain its date season and methods
absence of records is not proof of species absence without adequate evidence
licence conditions must be tied to actual species works and dates
reptile protection does not determine land ownership
licensing does not reserve development capacity
reptile compliance does not create access rights
no parcel reptile clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
